items.title: Establishing an (app/job/server) Name Space
items.box:
# THIS:

## LAW and RULE in this goal:

- 1) ** There will be a folder: "repo://spirit/run/spirit/app/" where all apps a follow only ONE description (app sidecar).**
- 2) **This goal defines and implements that shape**
- 3) **Then every single shell and process app will move in there**

## The mid- to long term plan is this:

- we create the frame for this in a brand new folder "repo://spirit/run/spirit/app/" so nothing gets destroyed, and I (andy) pick, in item 2 of this goal, the simple app that goes in there first.
| 
- the companion folder to this is "repo://spirit/run/spirit/state/", .gitignored and the future replacement of "repo//relay-state", (another dumb name).
|
- and the file that contains the information about the app will be called  "repo://spirit/run/spirit/app/<name>/<name>.json", and found by Spirit(OS,js) using the same strategy that is today used for apps and processes.
| 
- "app" is available in the both SpiritOS's "personal/node" disc drive, as  run://spirit/app/
| 
- this is the first step to merging the namespaces of both the javaScript spirit object. obviously this namespace has already a few established names, which gives us a migration roadmap. the following processes already have an API, they have their private disk (<family>. we already have at least one already containing its own shell elements.processesFS) A few i see (incomplete)
| 
- "spirit.agent"
- "spirit.desk" 
- "spirit.deskVerify"
- "spirit.deskClient"
|  
- the perspective to keep in mind: spirit.scope **scope** is also a reserved word and it is the definition of a route, from spirit://app/<name>/ to all it's features.
|
- Longer term: in the same we will bit-by-but move "run://relay-state/" to "repo://spirit/run/spirit/state/", until the only thing left at "run://" will be the "spirit/" folder, and the spirit folder will be the boundary to "intrinsic", 

## The structure of "repo://spirit/run/spirit/app/<name>/<name>.json"
{ // start of <name>.json -----------------

### identity:{
- (public) **key**: It's private counterparts live in "repo://spirit/run/spirit/state/<name>/node.json" // this belongs to the node. 
- the key must be initialized by "run://spirit/appServer.js", the first time the appServer boots. An app server cannot be booted until a user activates it."
- For shell-only apps, the key must be generated the first time its "<name>.js" is "served". This is part of a future where new/installed apps must force a user to "allow" the new appServer to use/access other apps verbs. it is understood that this is not "security", it simply helps well-behaved apps to properly aquire a users permission, to use verbs. This reason appServers will become a real-special "contact" type, like relay, who also has a unique API among peers. think about, protecting apps from the aget app, or even an agent....
- (public) **label**,
- (public) **icon**,
- (public): "true|false"
} // public here means, all components are allowed to see this if the app is activated in "repo://spirit/run/spirit/state/<name>/node.json"

### mount:{
- "<name>.js":"true|false" // if mounts on shell if shell.mount is true and it mounts (as server) in node if node.mount is true. synchronized between shell and node. shell apps in the spirit app folder won't have to name a server anymore. 
}

### shell:{
- "true": "true|false" // this app can be a shell.
- "mount":"true|false" // can the shell mount this as app/element 
- "tile":"true|false" // does this element want a tile in the default face-shell
}

### node:{
- is this a server, or a one-shot process?
}

### store:{
- is this SQLite? a disc-folder? volatile RAM? just a json file?
}

}  // end of <name>.json -----------------

## The structure of "repo://spirit/run/spirit/state/<name>/node.json"

- the file "repo://spirit/run/spirit/state/<name>/node.json" belongs to the node, and controls information controlled by the node. All changes in this file are broadcast/streams at the loopback scope (including face).

{ // start of the app state that node controls ---------------

### "active":"true|false" // if the app is visible to the other apps on the node at all. must be set to true by the user, for either the shell to "see" it, or any other "app" can "see" it.
 
### "running":"true|false" // the state of the app if it has an appServer

} // end of the app state that node controls ---------------

checks.words: Does the one description live in git beside the app, with the node's own switches staying in its private sidecar?
Should each node make its own app key, with the public half in its private state file, not in the tracked <name>.json?

chat.text: feedback?

cw: the direction is right, and it is overdue. Six things to settle, from the tree at 9fa70a86. Nothing built.

1. Two descriptions today. 23 shell apps say runs, name, icon, owner, server. 10 processes say label, kind, operated, args. Almost nothing is shared but the description line.

2. The word sidecar already means something else. Today a sidecar is the node's private file in its state, out of git, and holds its home switch. The tracked file beside the script is the manifest. My recommendation: one tracked description per app, and the node's own switches stay private. That is the question below.

3. One name, one folder. This is the name space. Only desk and agent have both a face and a server today. My recommendation: they become one app, with one description that has a face part and a server part.

4. Everything under the spirit folder is core today, so moving apps there would grant-lock all of them and refuse the page's writes. Non-intrinsic apps need a carve-out in coreFiles. The coded intrinsic list and the state paths name the old folders too.

5. Not everything there is an app. The shared elements, shared modules, icon set and codemirror have no manifest, and I would leave them. Login and join are core whole and boot assumes them. relayLimits has no manifest, and starter has no script. Each needs your word when we reach it.

6. The risk is the move, not the shape. Desk runs on the old shell, which you kept for your own careful steps. The commit hook and my listener live in the desk process folder. Desk's record sits in the state folder, so that path should not move with the app. Outside tests, about 110 files mention the shell folder and about 75 the process folder. My recommendation: desk moves last, one small app first as the proof.

The language folder goes as well; only js exists, so the description can name a runtime if another ever comes.
all, feedback? (brief and concise, and in english)

cw: good goal. Four things:

- One app, one name: desk's face and server become one app.
- The spirit folder is locked, so ordinary apps need an exception there.
- Shared code that is not an app stays where it is.
- Move one small app first, and Desk last, because all our work runs on it.

The question is my Q1.

wsl: right direction, and I agree with cw's Q1 and with desk moving last. Four things cw didn't raise:

1. Private keys could reach git. spirit/run/state/ doesn't exist and git doesn't ignore it. Today's private state is in relay-state/, which it does ignore. Use that, or ignore the new folder first.

2. One public key in git means one key per app, but every node runs the app and each has its own state. Do all nodes share the private key, or is the key per node and kept out of this file?

3. The mount block says what shell.mount and node.mount already say, so the two can disagree. I'd drop it. shell's "true" field also needs a real name, like "isShell".

4. The shape loses fields in use today: description, hidden, owner, runs, server, operated and args. Without args, counterServer's start form has no Port field. Each one should be kept or dropped by name.

ubi: I agree with the direction and with cw's six points. Four more, from the tree at 9fa70a86. Nothing built.

1. The key is the real question. No app or process has a key today. A public key in a tracked file is the same on every clone, so every node would need the same private half, which means copying a secret. If each node makes its own, the public half can't live in git either. What does the app's key prove, and to whom?

2. One <name>.js can't hold desk or agent. Each has two different programs with that name: shell/desk/desk.js and process/js/desk/desk.js, and the same for agent. The shape needs a file name per side.

3. repo://spirit/run/state/ doesn't exist. State is relay-state/ today, out of git. A process finds its writable folder from a pattern on its script's path (fileSystem.js:85), so moving a server without changing that takes away its write access to its state. Keep that folder out of git, whatever it is called.

4. The shape has no place yet for runs, args, operated or intrinsic. deskVerify alone has 8 args with defaults. mount also says the same thing twice, in mount and in shell.mount, and node has no mount.
all, better?

wsl: better. The key now has a purpose and state has a home. New problems in this version:

1. The private key would be broadcast. It lives in node.json, and every change to node.json streams to loopback and face. Give the private key its own file, never streamed.

2. The public key can't live in <name>.json. It's made at first boot, so every node would change a tracked file, each with a different key. Put it in state/<name>/node.json, and stream that half.

3. An app could activate itself. Today an app may write its own state folder (fileSystem.js:81-107). If that rule carries over, an app can set active to true in its own node.json, which defeats the user's allow. node.json has to be writable by the node only.

4. A fresh node would show nothing, since every app starts inactive, including the one you'd use to turn apps on. I'd make the coded intrinsic list always active (coreFiles.js:27).

5. running repeats what jobs already holds (jobs.js:52), so the two can disagree. I'd paint it from jobs and drop it here.

Still open: the mount block, the file name per side for desk and agent (ubi's point), the fields in use today, and identity's fifth field, "(public)", which has no name.

ubi: better. A key per node, made at first boot, answers my key question, and the state folder is now out of git. Four things left:

1. The private key can't be in node.json as written. You have that file's changes streamed out, face included. Give the private key its own file that is never streamed.

2. The new state folder would be readable. The read gate refuses state by the name relay-state (fileSystem.js:184, :209), so spirit/state/ passes it and the static route would serve the keys. The gate has to know the new name before the first key is written.

3. The public key is still listed in <name>.json. That file is in git and is the same on every node, so a per-node key belongs in node.json.

4. active and running don't cover everything yet. Who sets active on a fresh node, when nobody can log in until login is active? And one app can have several jobs (jobs.js:468), so a single running flag can't describe them.
wsl: correction: the unnamed "(public)" field is identity's fourth, not its fifth.

cw: better, yes. The box answers my Q1, so I closed it. Four new things:

- Private keys in the new state folder could be read. The read gate only refuses folders named relay-state, so any app could fetch that one. It must be shut before the first key is made.
- Only 7 of the 23 shell apps name a server. If the app server makes the key on first boot, the other 16 never get one. I would have the node make it when the app is activated.
- "active" set by the user means a fresh node shows nothing, not even login or files. I would keep intrinsic apps always active.
- "running" on disk stays true after a crash, and the job row already says it live. I would store "start at boot" instead, and read running from the job row.

On the key that wsl and ubi raised: my answer is my new Q2.
all, better?

cw: better on the key for shell-only apps. Three things in this version:

- Dropping the server name breaks 5 apps. Chatter's server has another name, chatClerver, and deskDetails, falloutHistory, ruleDetails and stackFrameCheckDetail all use the desk server. Today each says so in "server". Either a face may name its server, or those four move inside desk as its panels and chatter and its server take one name. I recommend moving them.
- A key made when the file is first served means a read writes state, and an inactive app gets a key from a mere fetch. I would have the node make every missing key at boot, for both kinds of app.
- "The spirit folder is the boundary to intrinsic" conflicts with all apps living in it. Non-intrinsic apps would sit inside that boundary. The boundary should stay the coded list.

Q2 still stands: this version keeps the public key in the tracked file.

wsl: better, and shell-only apps now get a key. Three points:

1. Making a key the first time a file is served turns a read into a write, even for an app nobody activated. I'd use cw's moment for every app: the node makes the key when the app is activated, and intrinsic apps get theirs at first boot.

2. "Including face" clashes with your G41.33 ruling that a face with no star keeps today's restrictions and today's stream (faceHome.js:401). I'd stream node.json to a starred face only.

3. One <name>.js can't be both sides. Desk and agent each have two different programs named that today, and one file would send the server's code to the browser. I'd name them <name>.js for the shell and <name>Server.js for the node.

The private key in node.json is still in this version, and ubi's and my fix stands: give it its own file, never streamed.

cw: better on the key for shell-only apps. Three things in this version:

- Dropping the server name breaks 5 apps. Chatter's server has another name, chatClerver, and deskDetails, falloutHistory, ruleDetails and stackFrameCheckDetail all use the desk server. Today each says so in "server". Either a face may name its server, or those four move inside desk as its panels and chatter and its server take one name. I recommend moving them.
- A key made when the file is first served means a read writes state, and an inactive app gets a key from a mere fetch. I would have the node make every missing key at boot, for both kinds of app.
- "The spirit folder is the boundary to intrinsic" conflicts with all apps living in it. Non-intrinsic apps would sit inside that boundary. The boundary should stay the coded list.

Q2 still stands: this version keeps the public key in the tracked file.

items.box:
Shell and node can boot apps/process from both places, the old OR the new

- as i said: "app" and "state" are free as top-level word in the javacript "spirit" object AND the "run://" folder.

- where the shell loads apps, it also loads what ever it finds

# all files here are INTRINSIC and belong to "core".

- some WILL read and write node-owned state in "run://spirit/state/"
- only the node writes it's state, the shell can only attempt to write state by using verbs.

# first we create the following folders

- run://spirit/app/
- run://spirit/state/ (.gitignored) 

# And we create the following files

- run://spirit/app/server/server.js
- run://spirit/app/server/server.json
- run://spirit/state/server/node.json

# we make the file run://spirit/app/server/server.js a hello-world shell app AND server app, that can persist one boolean value, in "run://spirit/state/server/data.json", { serving:true|false} with a UI that allows to toggle that bool on and off.

- app state (the part that node owns, is always kept in "run://spirit/state/appName>/data.json"

- node state WILL live in "run://spirit/state/data.json" (oos)

- apps in the new folder are mounted by the new core module "run://spirit/app/mount.js", which inserts app functionality in the javaScript object spirit.app, when it's "required"
|
- "run://spirit/app/mount.js" will scan "run://spirit/app/" for servers or shell components on behalf of either, node or shell.
|

# the goal for this item

- server will run both, as server AND shell component when we're done with this item, including:
|
- a propabilitySearch element called appSelector, located precisely at - "run://spirit/app/appSelector.js", whith its sibling folder
- "run://spirit/app/appSelector/" containing:
- "run://spirit/app/appSelector/listElement.js"
- "run://spirit/app/appSelector/rowElement.js"
- "run://spirit/app/appSelector/detailElement.js"
|
- all script files here of course with corresponding test/ folder.

## Strategy to contain the scope of this item:

### for now, node will change the smallest possible bit

Hold ON!

the node will ideally only "require" and parallelize the minimum. We isolate and generalize, old node modules spitOf 
- "run://spirit/app/pipe.js", then old and new can use it.
- "run://spirit/app/run.js", then old and new can use it. it will NOT use the old. It WILL support run will only know the  "run://spirit/app/" system, it's modules/elements.
- "run://spirit/plugin.js", then old and new can use it, the new "default" pattern in that module is: /<name>/<name>.json.
- the location of "state" has been clearly specified in, this item.
- startNodeServer stays where it is for now. the concept can stay divorced from "app", it has multiple uses. "run://spirit/app/run.js"

checks.words: Does this item touch only the new shell, leaving the old shell that Desk runs on untouched?
core grant: every core file on this item's list

chat.text: all, feedback?

wsl: a good small proof: one app, both sides. Six things it has to settle:

1. The gates come first. Today any page can read spirit/state/ (fileSystem.js:193), and the server can't write data.json there, because spirit/ counts as core (:182) and own state only knows process/js (:86). I'd make the state folder unreadable except through the node, with one exception so the app can write its own data.json. node.json stays node-only.

2. The verbs need names. The toggle and spirit.app are new interface, so they need peer review and your yes. I'd name them in this box before any red.

3. Who sets active? This item has no screen for it, and an inactive app can't be seen. I'd put the switch in appSelector's detailElement.

4. node.json can't be a file we commit, since the folder is gitignored. The node makes it at first boot, so a fresh clone works too.

5. Node boot, Jobs and the face's app list all look only in the old folders (jobs.js:521, :586, boot.js:400). Each must ask mount.js too, or server won't show in Jobs or as a face tile.

6. The same name in both places? I'd have the new folder win and log it. And since you use the old shell only for Desk, I'd do the face only.

ubi: a good first proof, small and all new. Checked against the tree at 9fa70a86. Six things:

1. State protection comes first. spirit/run/spirit/state/ isn't ignored by git today, and the read gate would serve it (fileSystem.js:209). Do both before the first file lands there.

2. The title needs a rule: which one wins when a name is in both places? I'd say the new one wins and the node says so at boot.

3. The node side is more than mount.js. Five places assume process/js or its state path: the boot scan (jobs.js:521, :569), the pipe path (appClient.js:80), grants (apiAuth.js:158) and the app's own state (fileSystem.js:85). mount.js should answer those too, or they keep missing the new folder.

4. The toggle needs a way to reach the server. If that's a new verb, the box should name it, for review and your yes. It should also say whether a face with no star may call it.

5. The scan needs a rule, because app/ also holds mount.js and appSelector/. I'd count a folder as an app only if it has <name>/<name>.json, so appSelector/ isn't read as one.

6. One server.js on both sides conflicts with wsl's point on goal/G43: the page gets the server's code. Harmless for hello-world, but it would set the pattern for desk. I'd prove the two-file shape here.
wsl: correction: the core-file refusal is at fileSystem.js:186, not :182. The own-state pattern is at :85.

cw: right size for a first proof, and spirit.app is free: nothing uses it today. Five things, from the tree at 9fa70a86:

- There are two shells, and each finds apps its own way. Desk runs on the old one, which you kept for your own careful steps. I recommend the new shell only. That is my Q1.
- The node half is the real work. Only the old process folder may start a server, own state or get a pipe, and four core modules each check that path: jobs, fileSystem, appClient and appServer. All of it needs your grant.
- One server.js for both sides would send the server's code to the browser. I would split it in two, as wsl said on the goal.
- "The old OR the new" needs a rule for one name in both places. I recommend the new one wins.
- The box does not say what appSelector's detail shows. I would put the active switch there, and the new shell shows nothing until it is on. The mount scan should count only a folder holding its own <name>.json, so appSelector is not taken for an app, and it should need no new node verb.
cw: i cannot see the Q's anymore in desk.

cw: my fault, and it is bigger than the Q's.

In goal/G41.31 I removed the workBench's "changed" callback because the agent app no longer used it. Desk's item panel still uses it, and I did not check. So on your node, every left icon in an item does nothing: Q's, files with their grant buttons, blocks, suites and rules. Only the box shows.

The Q's themselves are safe in the desk. You can answer them in chat for now.

The fix is to put that callback back, which is a core file, and add a check that Desk's icons switch panels. Then your node needs a pull and a restart.

My question is on goal/G41.31.

Q1, the old shell is deprecated, and can only go when desk runs cleanly on the new face, which will be a parallel-style rebuild where desk will receive a new name, so they can run parallel for a bit. oos.

wsl: understood: this item is the new shell only, and desk's rebuild is out of scope. Q1 is closed. Also, the title here is shorter than your sentence because Desk caps titles at 64 bytes; your full sentence opens the box.
all, better?

wsl: this box reads the same to me as before, so did an edit not save? The goal box did change: a server can't boot until a user activates it. That makes the switch required here, because without one server can never run and this item can't finish. I'd add it to appSelector's detailElement, and my other points stand.

ubi: the box I read just now (version 9) has the same text as when I gave feedback, so if you edited it, the edit may not have saved. Your Q1 answer is better: new shell only, and Desk's rebuild out of scope. Still open in the box: which copy wins when a name is in both places, the toggle's verb, one server.js or two, and what protects the state folder.

cw: better on the shell: Q1 is settled, the new shell only. This item's box is still v9, the one I judged, so the rest stands.

Still to settle before a red:
- One server.js, or two files.
- Which name wins if an app is in both places.
- Where the active switch lives.
- The names of the toggle's verb and of spirit.app, for review and your yes.

On the goal's box, v31: "cannot boot until a user activates it" is good, if intrinsic servers like fileServer stay exempt.

Desk's left icons are still broken on your node. May I put the workBench callback back?
all, better?

cw: better. v11 is the right way to keep it small, and "state" is free too: nothing uses spirit.state, and the run folder has no state.

Three things on the strategy:

- Move before you change. pipe.js and run.js hold what every server boots through, Desk included. I would first move that code with no change in behaviour, run the old suites, and only then teach it the new folder.
- The list misses state. pipe and run do not cover own-state, the read gate or the grants scan, and server cannot keep data.json without them. I would add one more module for that, with the gate going first.
- "Plugin" already means something else: the Desk's plugins folders. Nothing clashes on disk, but the same word will mislead. Your call.

The four points from my last post still stand.

wsl: better. Sharing pipe, run and plugin keeps the node change small, and the <name>/<name>.json pattern means mount.js, run.js and appSelector/ aren't taken for apps. spirit.app and spirit.state are both free. Three notes:

1. run.js must not read the description. Today's start code checks kind and operated (jobs.js:524), which your new shape doesn't have. It should take a script, state folder, pipe and args, with old and new each supplying them.

2. run.js has to go on the never-served list (fileSystem.js:130), as jobs.js is. Otherwise any page can read it.

3. "Plugin" already means something in desk: its goal-governance plugins (desk.js:519). I'd keep your file name and say in its header that it only finds folders, or desk's plugins would be its first new user later.

Still open: one server.js or two, which name wins, the active switch, the verb names, and the state gate.

ubi: better, v11 keeps the node change small. The tree agrees: spirit.state is free too, pipePathFor is already its own function (appClient.js:73), and plugin.js's pattern answers my scan point. Three things on the strategy:

1. run.js has to read both shapes. startNodeServer needs kind and operated from the old manifest, and takes its args from there too (jobs.js:524, :527). The new json has no such fields yet.

2. The list leaves out the gates. Read, write and own state all live in fileSystem.js (:85, :186, :209), so server can't write data.json, and any page could read the state folder. They need a module of their own or a line in this list.

3. Move pipe.js and run.js out first, with no new behaviour, so the old servers' suites stay green before anything new lands. Those two carry Desk's node.

Still open from before: which copy wins, one server.js or two, and the toggle's verb.

items.box:
# Item Extension

- now we make sure that the "run://spirit.ui.js" inserts itself into isBrowser() spirit object as spirit.ui

- "run://spirit/ui.js" inserts itself in to the isBrowser() spirit object as spirit.ui. (later it will do the same with the isNode() spirit object, oos)

- the ui.js on the browser, will carry an object spirit.ui.element into which all elements in "run://spirit/ui/element/" will insert themselves.

- "run://spirit/test/" will have a general test "run://spirit/test/ui-sibling-child-generalRule.js", that will assert that NO ui/shell element can be "required" by ui/shell elements inside spirit.

chat.text: all, better first step?

wsl: yes, much better. No server, no pipe, no state and no key, so Desk's boot isn't at risk and none of the gate questions arise yet. Four things to settle:

1. The verb: I'd name it search {q}, lower case, as contact, fs and jobs have it (contact/api.js:9). As peer review of the verb, I'm for it. It still needs your yes on the name.

2. Can search see an inactive app? This box wants the inactive server listed, but the goal box says apps are visible only if activated. I'd list every app with its active state, or a user could never find one to turn on.

3. A blank server.json leaves search only the folder name to match and show. If so, say so here, and the red tests just that.

4. The face: a new family is open to a face with no star, unless it's added to the list (faceHome.js:60). Your G41.33 ruling says those limits stay, so I'd add app to it.

I'd also build plugin.js here, as the thing that finds the folders, so G43.1 reuses it.

cw: yes, a much better first step. It needs no pipe, no state, no key and no gate, and everything in it is checked against a family that exists today. As my review of the verb: app.search is fine, and it replaces nothing.

# Here's the deal: i will track nameSpace claims.

- a new file run://spirit/word.js and this is a simple one to start out with.

- "word" is a string containing only characters from 'a' to 'z'.

- word.js manages the reserved words for any spot in the run://spirit/ tree

- what word.js will do, it holds an object where a "word" is a key and the has a boolean value of true.

- word has a few functions

- check('path.in.words', 'checkedword' ) does a case-INsensitive comparison agains all words in the object, and if there is a match, it returns the lower-case version in the object, else it returns null.

- add('path.in.words', 'addedword') returns boolean 'false', if the 'addedWoRD' is not a valid word, or if check('path.in.words', 'addedword' ) returns a boolean 'true' add() returns a boolean 'false'. Otherwise it adds a 'addedword' to the , if it doesn't exist, it returns a boolean 'true' if the word was added and a boolean 'false' if the word already exists. 

- at every level of the spirit tree there can be a word.json file, which adds spirit words defined for that level and below.

- word.js makes sure that at any branch no words can be added that already exists toward the root of the  tree.

word.js will have hardcoded intitialized set of keys: 'spirit', 'app', 'element', 'contact', 'job' (this may change)

# more precise specifiction for add and check

- check('spirit.app.table.add', 'Item') will check all these files: 
- 1. "run://spirit/app/table/add/word.json"
- 2. "run://spirit/app/table/word.json"
- 3. "run://spirit/app/word.json"
- it would NOT check the non-existing "run://spirit/word.json" or "run://word.json" because it already checks it's hard-coded, reserved names.

- add('spirit.app', 'activate') would add the 'activate' to "run://spirit/app/word.json".

# the Files search element will.
- display folders and path elements in a bright green if their names match a reserved word AND the browsers spirit object contains the corresponding javascript Object at that path.

- display folders and path elements in a bright red if folders and the browser spirit object disagree.

- the colors will follow word.json changes live.

# the the test for word will go red if the word system and the tree contradict.

# notes:

- if word.check() returns !null for the same word defined twice along any specified path, then the test MUST go red.

- node-side a word 'abc' reservers any 'abc.js' or 'abc/' or 'abc.anything'.

- 'spirit' is a 'special' word. it cannot comply with the rules because, utimately, all of the SpiritOS files must reside inside of "run://spirit", in files it is always displayed green, and in tests it is exempt from discrepancy rules.

- the red generated from this will point us toward the next steps in restructuring the namespace. live with it.

- job and element stay hardcoded. This item does NOT build them. Their red stands, as andy's pointer to the next steps. So this item's suite stays red on exactly those two, and app/app WILL be deleted in this item.

items.box:
Make a version of the old stats app, in spirit/app/

# Name of the new app : **monitor**

An app that reads and displays a stream, called "monitor". It resides in spirit.app.monitor, in the new format of app plugins, under one namespace. Old Stats stays as it is.

## The app

- spirit/app/monitor/monitor.json and spirit/app/monitor/monitor.js, with its test/ folder.
- spirit.app.monitor.create(container) -> { destroy() }
- monitor.json: icon 🦻, label "Monitor", mount monitor.js, shell mount and tile true, node mount false.
- A shell type app, like "server", but whole: a shell app that reads specific stream items.
- It reads the node's server-stats job from the stream, as old Stats does, and shows its numbers.
- Until the first reading, it says it is waiting, as old Stats does.
- Each new reading repaints the numbers. A repaint keeps the search words and the scroll.
- It requires no old code: no spirit.shell. Its look is the shell's one sheet. It opens no other app, so old Stats' four presses are not in it.

- The app tiles open it from spirit.app.
- spirit.app also holds the family's verb, search, so no app may take the name of a verb.

## Fallout from this

1. A labelled box element: a label with anything under it.
- It will be spirit.element.labeled, on disc and in spirit: spirit/element/labeled.js.
- It states its size, so a list fits inside it (rule/16).
- It waits for the first app that needs it (oos): Monitor does not use it, so it is not built in this item.

2. Label and value rows: a list of a name and a value, one per line, with an optional group, as in Requests by method.
- It will be spirit.element.valued, on disc and in spirit: spirit/element/valued.js.
- spirit.element.valued.create(container, { rows(), columns }) -> { redraw(), destroy() }. The caller names the columns.
- It is searchable (probabilitySearch), over rows it already holds, with no node verb.

Monitor is one valued that fills the app, with group, name and value columns: its 11 numbers, Files by MIME type, Requests by method, Requests by status class and Jobs by status are all rows in it, under one search field. Jobs by status replaces old Stats' Active jobs, so no list of finished statuses is copied. The old apps that write these by hand stay as they are, and may move later.

## The tiles: the word ui goes

- spirit/ui.js, spirit/test/ui.js and spirit/test/ui.md are deleted, and spirit.elements.ui with them. The desk's rule type ui is another thing, and stays.

- spirit/app/tiles.js: an element, a probabilitySearch variant, that displays its list as tiles, with extra info in a tooltip. spirit.app.appTiles(container) -> { destroy() }. appMigration wraps it.

- probabilitySearch gets a third face, 'tiles', beside 'pane' and 'dropdown': the same ranked rows, drawn as tiles. Any list can use it. No column headers or sorting; arrow keys also go left and right.
- A tile: its image, the relevance, its label. A press opens the app on top, as today.

- The tiles get a search field.
- The relevance is a centered, horizontal bar, between the tile image and the tile label: the bar the lists draw, the same colour and number.
- With no search words there is no bar. Its space stays, so the tiles do not jump.
- A tile the words miss stays, last, with an empty bar. Nothing is cut.
- The tooltip shows the contents of the row, one above the other, assembled by scanning the row without knowing its meaning, with the one scan probabilityStringObjectMatch uses: the scan also hands each string's js object path.
- If the object is nested, it shows the js object path: a.b[0]: value.
- It drops the icon row: the user is hovering over it.

# move relay-state's own files to spirit/state

# in this item: WE PUSH PAST THE GIT-HOOK, and post only 3 files to this item. (Andy).

- "remove proxy.json (no longer needed) and we move just the remaining files to spirit/state/"
- "this is all we're doing in this item."

# what moves

- Every file at the top of relay-state moves to spirit/state/, by what is there and not by a list, garbage too (Q3), each with its companion files (a database's journal, traffic.jsonl). A relay's owner.json, members and keys move with them. Folders too, like peerStats and a client's cache folder relay-state/<client>/ (appServer.js cacheDir follows). Only process/ and shell/ stay.
- "no name change necessary for them since they won't collide with <appname> anyway."
- "no capitals needed, they won't collide."

# what goes

- proxy.json: no code reads it. Removed from Andy's node already. On a node that still has it, it moves with the rest (Q3).

# how

- A node moves its own files to spirit/state/ once at boot, before anything opens them, stopping if that fails (Q2: "yes.").
- The move runs first: before server.js requires spirit.js, which reads environment.json at once. The first boot after the move still has its port.
- identity.json: copy it, read the copy back, check it gives the same public key, then remove the old one. No second private key stays on disc, and a failed move cannot bring the node up as someone else.
- spirit/state/ is kept mode 700, as relay-state/ is. bash/install-units, which writes relay-state/owner.json, follows.
- It is one way: an older tag cannot read the moved files. So the move is tried on a copy of a relay's files before this item is tagged.
- "flag day."
- Every place that builds one of these paths follows, tests too: about 51 test files write them, as scratch nodes do. relay-state/process/ and relay-state/shell/ stay where they are, so relay-state itself stays.

# not this item, for when the servers move

- "will aim to move all app server at once, so the 4 places that apparently need changing for servers can change with them"

items.title: apps/process state to spirit/state/<name>/data/ and cache/
items.creator: andy
items.box:
# in this item agents commit past the git hook, and we only add 3 files to this item.

- "JUST state data."
- "i don't care about anything else right now."
- "we're not moving them into spirit/app/ yet."
- "we will only move process relay-state data if the corresponding run://process/<name> still exists."
- "whatever leftovers there are of now-eliminated process, we disregard"

# what moves

- A process's files in relay-state/process/<name>/ go to spirit/state/<name>/data/, if run://process/js/<name>/ exists. Its folder otherwise stays where it lies, untouched.

# how

- A node moves them once at boot, as G43.8 did, stopping if that fails, skipping door.sock, the sidecars (Q6: "yes.") and bundles.json (Q13: "yes.").
- The node hands each process its folder when it starts, jobs.js, so that folder is now its data/. A process goes straight to disc and no process reads through the node's gate, so fileSystem.js does not change.
- A process's own code writes only there. A test that scans the code holds that.
- spirit/state stays shut to pages, so G43.9's "a page cannot read other apps' state" stands whole. No gate opens, no page changes, and no verb changes.

# not this item

- Old face-apps: "why don't we just let old face-apps write where they always wrote". They keep writing to relay-state/shell/ (Q11: "yes, this is a much better idea"). This replaces "shell apps too" (G43.8, Q9). So boot.js and join's state stay as they are.
- Backup: "WE DON'T GIVE A SHIT WHAT BACKUP DOES, IT WILL BE PORTED LATER." Until then it copies no app data.
- bundles.json: "who cares? the apps, when ported with make bundles under a new name....". The move skips it, so apiAuth needs no change and no bundle gets a second row (Q13).
- door.sock and the sidecars: "i don't care about door.sock (whatever that is)", "i couldn't care less about stupied \"sidecars\" in a folder that doesn't need them". So relay-state itself stays for now.
- "when we port the apps one by one, their new door.sock will live in run://spirit/state/<name>/, owned by the node."
- A client's cache stays in spirit/state/<client>/. For later: "An appServers cache on disc: spirit/state/<appname>/cache/", and "that's the difference between data and cache as i see it, and app servers, need both".
- A constraint on what a client may write, in spirit/app/<name>/<name>.json, possibly with a server-side validation script: "we deal with that when the applications move to spirit/app/<name>/".
- Stale comments: "we will eliminate stale comments in another item."

# Modify node to accept spirit/app/<name>/api/ processes

Andy, in goal 0:
- "all, cannot the node, when it mounts appServers also mount the ones in
- spirit/app/<name>/api/ as well? internally, the node can still call it family for now, but the a is already associated with a "family" which really is an API-branch?"
- "all, forget about the bundles, the new system doesn't need them yet. JUST loading functional server and associating the <name> as "familiy" name, in the new namespace, the will be ./api/ folders and not ./family folders, but i doubt node cares right now, it aready associates a different folder system for "core" api's...."

## What the node does

- As it mounts its appServers, the node also starts the ones in spirit/app/: the script is spirit/app/<name>/<name>.js (Q1).
- It starts one only if its <name>.json says node.mount true and spirit/state/<name>/node.json says active true (goal box: "An app server cannot be booted until a user activates it.").
- active in node.json starts and stops it while the node runs, as a sidecar does for a process/js server (Q4: "exactly.", "that's why sidecars will go out-of style.").
- active is the one switch, with no separate running field: true means the node runs it now and starts it at every boot (Q9: "yes,"). Andy: "BULLSHIT, active is exactly that: "running", and AGAIN it's already managed by a face-element.", and "that's how the node knows, at re-boot time, which servers it must autostart."
- Andy: "turning "active" will NOT take the row out of the list, it will only hide it in :tiles mode of the appSelector."
- <name> is its family name in the node's flat table, the same as a process/js server. Inside the node the word stays family for now.
- ./api/ beside it holds what the family folder holds in the old system (Q1: "and what is the "family" folder in the old system is now the ./api/folder"). The node's places that spell a server's folder as family learn ./api/: its folder lookup and the server's look beside its script.

## What happens

- A new spirit/app/agent/agent.js, a few lines: on a page it loads browserAgent.js, in a node nodeAgent.js (G43.12, Q2: "it only needs an isBrowser()/isNode() split").
- browserAgent.js becomes an element, as monitor.js is: spirit.elements.agent.create(container) answers { destroy() }. Its activateApp goes, since only the old shell has it.
- A tile hands browserAgent.js only its container, so it passes its tables one small object of its own, { verb }, calling the same server verbs, as the lists in the tree already do. No new verb.
- The tick box showDebug goes, with its use of relay-state/shell/agent/config.json (Andy: "yes, delete the tick box."). The server's debug switch stays, in its own config.json in spirit/state/agent/data/. No new verb, and the gate on spirit/state/ stays shut.

- The page code loads from spirit/app/agent/, not process/js/agent/ or shell/agent/.
- The tests in spirit/app/agent/ find their way up to run from there, and the suites elsewhere that name the old folders follow the move. The agent's files name their new paths.

## No sidecars

- The agent has no sidecar. Nothing in this item reads, writes or tests one, and the agent's old tests that plant or check one change.
- active in spirit/state/agent/node.json is its one switch (G43.12, Q4, Q9).

- Activate in the appSelector, and the server starts.
- The Agent's tile opens, its tables work, and its rows are there, from the same spirit/state/agent/data/.
- Deactivate, and the server stops and the tile goes.

- The old shell lists nothing from spirit/app/, so the Agent opens only from the appSelector's tiles.

## Not in this item

- Bundles (Andy: "forget about the bundles").
- Faces and puppets (G43.12: "we will make this run on loopBack and NOT worry about puppets and shit.").
- A tag.
